title: Long TSM — AI Wafer Monopoly Re-Entry After KOSPI Contagion Flush
entry: Enter $435–460 (TSM ADR at ~$443 pre-market June 24, down 3-5% from $467.67 June 23 close on overnight Nikkei and Taiwanese market contagion from the KOSPI rout). Scale: 60% on June 24 open at $435-455 if market stabilizes post-NVDA Annual Meeting; 40% add on any further dip to $425-435 if June 24 session is broadly risk-off. Do NOT add below $420 — below that level the June 23 rout is structural, not technical. Conditional: de-risk 50% of position if NVDA Annual Meeting today at noon ET delivers cautious AI demand commentary AND Micron Q3 tonight guides Q4 below $33B.
stop_loss: $420 daily close (~6.0% below $447 entry midpoint) — implies the AI wafer demand thesis has been structurally impaired, not just temporarily displaced: either NVDA has materially reduced Blackwell ramp guidance, Samsung has won meaningful NVDA AI chip production share from TSM at the 3nm node, OR the BofA 3-hike rate path has caused hyperscalers to formally announce capex reductions that reduce 2026-27 wafer demand
targets: $490 — TSM ADR recovers to pre-KOSPI-rout level ($467.67 June 23 close +4.8%); NVDA Annual Meeting and MU Q3 both clear positively, restoring AI semiconductor demand narrative; +9.6% from $447 midpoint

$520 — TSM beat-and-raise when it reports Q2 revenue (July 17, 2026); revenue consensus $28.8B; if 3nm/4nm Blackwell wafer revenue accelerates above plan and TSM raises full-year guidance, stock re-rates; +16.3%

$560 — blue sky: TSM announces 2nm capacity expansion ahead of schedule in response to NVDA-confirmed $1T AI orders through 2027; sell-side upgrades to $600 PT; AI wafer shortage re-priced structurally higher; +25.3%
catalyst: Two sequential catalysts today: (1) NVDA Annual Meeting at 9 AM PT / noon ET — Jensen Huang's AI demand commentary is the definitive real-time signal on TSM's Blackwell wafer demand; (2) Micron Q3 tonight — a beat-and-raise confirms DRAM/HBM4 capacity is fully absorbed, validating TSM's foundry utilization at the HBM stacking node. Separately, TSM reports Q2 FY2026 revenue on July 17; consensus expects $28.8B (+38% YoY), and the company's 3nm/4nm capacity that serves Blackwell GPU production is fully booked. TSM's previous opportunity (long-tsm-foundry-ai-wafer-demand-2026-05-26) was a target_hit, confirming the thesis is structurally intact.
thesis:
Taiwan Semiconductor is the only company in the world that can manufacture NVDA's Blackwell and Vera Rubin AI chips, AMD's MI300 series, and Apple's A18 Pro at the volumes hyperscalers and OEMs require. This production monopoly at the 4nm/3nm node is the single most defensible competitive position in the global semiconductor supply chain. The KOSPI-driven -3% to -5% overnight decline in TSM's ADR is pure contagion: TSM has no South Korean exposure, no Samsung overlap in its AI foundry business, and no direct linkage to the MSCI index flows that caused the June 23 KOSPI rout.

The prior TSM opportunity (target_hit on long-tsm-foundry-ai-wafer-demand-2026-05-26) confirms the thesis plays out predictably through AI chip cycle catalysts. Jensen Huang's stated $1 trillion in AI order visibility through 2027 — cited at GTC 2026 March — requires TSM to expand N3/N4 capacity substantially above current plan. The July 17 Q2 earnings report will be the next fundamental catalyst, but today's NVDA Annual Meeting and tonight's MU Q3 are the two near-term events that could restore the rout-driven discount.

The bull case for re-entry here is asymmetric: if both today's catalysts clear positively, TSM ADR recovers from $443 to $467+ within 1-2 sessions (+5%), then continues to $490 as the AI semis rout is confirmed as transient. If both catalysts disappoint (NVDA cautious, MU misses), the stop at $420 (-6%) limits the downside. The 1:3.4 R/R reflects this asymmetry — the positive scenario has more force than the negative because TSM's fundamentals are literally unchanged by the KOSPI rout.

The structural counter-argument is geopolitical: Taiwan risk premium has compressed dramatically since the Iran ceasefire removed the world's 'risk-on, risk-off' focal point, but the underlying China-Taiwan tension is a latent tail risk that re-priced sharply in 2022. A China escalation scenario would permanently impair TSM's value as a listed ADR, independent of AI wafer demand. This tail risk is why conviction is medium (not high) and position size 3% (not 5-6%).
bull_case: NVDA Annual Meeting delivers explicit AI demand confirmation: Jensen reiterates '$1T in orders through 2027' and explicitly says Blackwell/Vera Rubin production is on schedule with no supply constraints. Micron Q3 beats $36B revenue AND Q4 guides above $37B, confirming HBM4 demand. TSM ADR gaps up 5-7% on June 25 open to $465-480, recovering the full KOSPI discount. TSM Q2 earnings on July 17 beat revenue consensus, raising full-year guidance. TSM to $520 by mid-July.
bear_case: NVDA Annual Meeting delivers cautious commentary on AI capex pull-forward risk ('hyperscalers are evaluating their 2027 roadmaps'; 'we're monitoring tariff impacts on data center CapEx decisions'). Micron Q3 guides Q4 below $34B on Samsung HBM4E competition. TSM ADR breaks below $443 intraday and closes at $435; position is partially de-risked per the conditional rule. If TSM closes below $420 on a second session, the stop is triggered.
invalidation: $420 daily close; OR NVDA Annual Meeting explicitly warns of AI capex reduction from any hyperscaler (Microsoft, Google, Meta, Amazon all cited as reducing AI infrastructure spend); OR TSM Q2 revenue guidance (July 17) misses consensus by >5% ($27.4B or below); OR Samsung announces a qualified 3nm AI chip foundry alternative to TSM that achieves a >5% share of NVDA Blackwell production
